source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Biological Foundation Models

page_placements.theme: Non-additive effects of joint ablation (within heads, across layers, between head groups)

record.file_problem: None noted; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses the Hydra effect and reports its own results on non-additivity in biological-model activation patching, but it does not measure downstream compensation or test any listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The post cites Hydra effect and backup-head work as examples of non-additivity; those cited findings are not rows. Its own non-additivity and ranking results are recorded as related findings, but they do not show later components restoring a prediction after an ablation. The synthetic Shapley comparison is about the performance of an alternative ranking method, not a measurement of self-repair.
record.test_reason: The study is about single-cell biological transformers (Geneformer, scGPT). It measures aggregate non-additivity in activation patching and how it affects component rankings. It never ablates a component and measures later components restoring the output, so it does not isolate self-repair. It cites the Hydra effect and backup heads only as examples of non-additivity. No version is tested. V7 is closest, but the ranking bias comes from interactions in general, not from self-repair shown as compensation, and the setting is not language models.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The author also argues that the non-additivity bias is likely relevant to LLM interpretability. He recommends reporting residual non-additivity, computing ranking certificates, and using Shapley-based alternatives.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mediation archives, a non-additivity decomposition, and ranking certificates in biological transformers; it does not perform the original claim's component-ablation and downstream-compensation measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that empirical severity in LLMs could differ by architecture; no LLM comparison is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower bounds on non-additivity were positive in 10 of 16 run-pairs, with a median lower-bound ratio to total effect of 0.725.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In biological transformers, interactions among components account for a substantial share of the total patching effect, beyond measurement noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Under structural-bias assumptions, the fraction of certifiable pairwise rankings collapsed by an order of magnitude or more.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-component patching rankings in biological transformers are largely not robust to interaction-induced bias.

fits_no_version.finding: In Geneformer V2-316M, ablating the top 5 to 50 TRRUST-aligned heads caused no significant drop in perturbation prediction, although those heads gave 23x larger logit shifts than random heads. Ablating 20 random heads caused a significant drop. The author reads this as distributed, redundant computation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-relevant computation in single-cell transformers is distributed and redundant, so ablating heads chosen for biological alignment does not degrade the task.

record.problems: The empirical non-additivity results are from biological transformers, not language models. The specific model or checkpoint for the mediation archives is not stated in the post, and the exact fraction of rankings certified is not given. The results do not measure downstream compensation or prediction restoration.
record.rows_left_out: No related findings omitted under the row limit. Cited Hydra/backup-head results were excluded because they are findings from other work; the synthetic Shapley comparison was excluded because it evaluates an alternative ranking method rather than measuring self-repair.

untested.parts: No single attention-layer ablation followed by a measure of later-layer compensation.
No measure of late-MLP downregulation of the top token, and no change in it after earlier ablation.
Heads are ablated, but only task degradation is measured, not compensation on the output distribution.
No per-prompt compensation or overcorrection measure.
No backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons studied.
No comparison of mean or resample ablation against zero ablation for compensation.
Ranking bias is attributed to general non-additivity. It is not attributed to self-repair, and the models are not language models.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' subject should be read as Geneformer and scGPT. The 316M figure belongs to Geneformer V2, and the post does not say which model the mediation archives come from. The head-ablation result (Section 5.3) concerns task reliance, not compensation, so it bears on no version. The synthetic Shapley comparison is correctly excluded, since it evaluates the author's own method.

versions.untested_parts: No layer ablation followed by measurement of later attention-layer compensation or prediction restoration.
No measurement of late-MLP downregulation of a maximum-likelihood token or its change after earlier-component ablation.
No single-head ablation test of compensation on the output distribution across general text, model families, or sizes.
No prompt-level measurement of compensation variability or overcorrection.
No test of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as self-repair mechanisms.
No comparison of on-distribution mean or resample ablations with zero ablation.
The post studies ranking bias from non-additivity, but does not test whether self-repair specifically causes ablation-based importance scores to misstate a component's role.
